name: VO2max 5x5 (115%)
desc: Five 5-minute intervals at 115% FTP with equal recovery. Settle into a high, sustainable cadence and aim to finish every rep at the same power. Builds maximal aerobic power and time spent near VO2max.

name: VO2max 5x5 (short rest)
desc: Harder progression of the 5x5: 115% FTP with only 4 minutes of recovery between reps. The last two reps will feel near maximal; keep cadence above 95 rpm to spare the legs. For riders already comfortable with 5x5 at 115% and full rest.

name: VO2max Intro 3x5
desc: Entry-level VO2max session: three 5-minute efforts at 112% FTP with 5 minutes easy between. Learn to pace long VO2 intervals without blowing up in the first minute. Good first block of VO2 work.

name: VO2max 4x4
desc: Four 4-minute intervals at 118% FTP with 3 minutes active recovery. Breathing should be maximal by the end of each rep. A time-efficient, well-researched protocol for raising VO2max.

name: VO2max 6x3
desc: Six 3-minute intervals at 120% FTP with 3 minutes recovery. Shorter reps allow a slightly higher intensity while still accumulating 18 minutes near VO2max. Keep cadence high and smooth.

name: Long VO2 3x8
desc: Three 8-minute intervals at 106% FTP with 4 minutes recovery. Slightly lower intensity than classic VO2 work but much more time at high oxygen uptake; the final minutes of each rep should feel very hard. Research favourite for well-trained riders.

name: Long VO2 4x8
desc: Harder progression of the long-interval set: four 8-minute reps at 107% FTP with only 2 minutes recovery, as in the original study. Pace evenly; this is a deep aerobic stimulus with substantial accumulated fatigue.

name: 30/30s Intro
desc: Two sets of ten 30-second efforts at 125% FTP with 30 seconds easy between. Oxygen uptake stays high across the set even though each rep is short. A forgiving way to accumulate VO2max time.
src: Billat 2001 30-30 intermittent running, adapted for cycling

name: 30/30s 3x12
desc: Three sets of twelve 30/30s at 130% FTP with 5 minutes between sets. Hit each ON at a high cadence and spin lightly through the OFF. Accumulates 18 minutes of hard work around VO2max.

name: 30/30s 4x8
desc: Four sets of eight 30/30s at 130% FTP, 4 minutes easy between sets. Shorter sets help keep quality high on every repetition. Targets VO2max and repeated high-power tolerance.

name: 30/15s 3x13
desc: Three sets of thirteen 30-second efforts at 125% FTP with 15-second recoveries, 3 minutes easy between sets. The short recovery keeps oxygen uptake near maximal for most of each 9.75-minute set. Proven to outperform equal-work long intervals in trained cyclists.

name: 30/15s 2x13
desc: Easier introduction to 30/15s: two sets of thirteen 30-second efforts at 120% FTP with 15-second recoveries. Use it before progressing to three sets. Builds VO2max with less total load.

name: 40/20s 3x8
desc: Three sets of eight 40-second efforts at 120% FTP with 20 seconds easy, 5 minutes between sets. Recovery is short, so oxygen uptake climbs quickly and stays high. A staple for raising aerobic ceiling and repeatability.

name: 40/20s 3x10
desc: Harder 40/20 session: three sets of ten at 125% FTP. Expect the final reps of each set to be very hard. For riders who can already complete 3x8 cleanly.

name: VO2max Pyramid
desc: Intervals of 1-2-3-4-3-2-1 minutes with equal recovery; shorter reps are ridden harder (125%) and longer ones at 115%. Gives varied VO2max stimulus with a mental focus on the 4-minute peak. 16 minutes of total work.

name: Fast-Start VO2 Intervals
desc: Five 5-minute intervals that start with 30 seconds at 145% FTP and then settle at 110%. The hard start drives oxygen uptake up quickly so more of each rep is spent near VO2max. 4 minutes recovery between reps.

name: Tabata 2 Sets
desc: Two Tabata sets: eight 20-second all-out efforts (target about 170% FTP) with 10 seconds rest, 10 minutes easy between sets. ERG is released for the efforts; go as hard as you can each time. Hits both anaerobic capacity and VO2max in very little time.

name: Tabata ERG Held
desc: Tabata structure with power held in ERG at 150% FTP instead of all-out: three sets of eight 20/10s, 6 minutes easy between sets. A more controlled, repeatable version that still pushes anaerobic tolerance hard.

name: 1-Minute Repeats 8x
desc: Eight 1-minute efforts at 135% FTP with 2 minutes easy. Each rep should feel very hard by 40 seconds. Develops anaerobic capacity and the ability to bridge gaps or survive short climbs.

name: 1-Minute Repeats 10x
desc: Ten 1-minute efforts at 145% FTP with 2 minutes recovery, split into two blocks of five. A demanding anaerobic session with high lactate levels. For riders already completing the 8x version.

name: 2-Minute Repeats
desc: Six 2-minute efforts at 125% FTP with 4 minutes recovery. Sits between VO2max and anaerobic capacity; expect heavy legs and maximal breathing at the end of each rep. Great for short climbs and race-winning moves.

name: Micro-Bursts 15/15
desc: Three sets of ten 15-second bursts at 150% FTP with 15 seconds easy, 5 minutes between sets. Quick, punchy accelerations that teach the body to clear lactate while repeatedly recruiting fast-twitch fibres.

name: Micro-Bursts Intro
desc: Easier micro-burst session: two sets of ten 15/15s at 140% FTP with 6 minutes between sets. Focus on snappy accelerations and relaxed recoveries. A good introduction before the full 3-set version.

name: Anaerobic Ladder
desc: Efforts of 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 seconds with power falling as duration rises (150% down to 125%), then back down. Full recoveries of about 3 minutes keep quality high. Trains anaerobic capacity across the durations of attacks and short climbs.

name: Standing Sprints 8x15s
desc: Eight 15-second all-out standing sprints with almost 5 minutes easy spinning between. Jump hard out of the saddle and drive to the line. Full recovery means every sprint should be close to peak power.

name: Neuromuscular 10s Sprints
desc: Ten 10-second maximal sprints with 3 minutes recovery. Very short efforts focus purely on peak power and fibre recruitment without much fatigue. Stay seated for the first half, then stand to finish.

name: Sprint Pyramid
desc: All-out sprints of 10, 15, 20, 30, 20, 15 and 10 seconds with 4-5 minutes easy between. Longer sprints test sprint endurance, shorter ones peak power. Treat each one as a race finish.

name: Long Sprints 6x30s
desc: Six 30-second all-out sprints with 5 minutes recovery. These test sprint endurance: power will fade in the final 10 seconds, so keep driving. Useful for long sprints and late-race attacks.

name: Big-Gear Starts
desc: Eight 12-second sprints started from low cadence (about 60 rpm) in a heavy gear, 4 minutes between. Builds torque and the ability to accelerate from slow speeds out of corners or on climbs.

name: Lead-Out Sprints
desc: Six race-style finishes: 1 minute at 110% FTP simulating the lead-out train, then a 15-second all-out sprint, with 5 minutes recovery. Teaches you to sprint from fatigue at race speed.

name: Endurance with Sprints
desc: Ninety minutes of steady endurance at 65% FTP with a 15-second sprint every 5 minutes for the middle hour. Combines aerobic base work with neuromuscular stimulus. Keep sprints sharp; keep the endurance truly easy.

name: Seated Climbs 65rpm
desc: Four 10-minute seated climbs at 88% FTP and 65 rpm with 5 minutes easy spinning at normal cadence. Stay seated, keep the upper body still and push through the whole pedal stroke. Builds climbing-specific muscular endurance.

name: Long Seated Climbs 60rpm
desc: Three 15-minute seated climbs at 85% FTP and 60 rpm with 5 minutes recovery. Simulates long steady gradients where cadence naturally drops. Focus on smooth torque and relaxed breathing.

name: Climbing with Standing Surges
desc: Three 8-minute climbs at 85% FTP and 70 rpm, each with a 30-second standing surge at 120% every 2 minutes. Recover seated straight after each surge without dropping the pace. Mimics changes of rhythm on a climb.

name: Hill Repeats 8x3
desc: Eight 3-minute hill repeats at 108% FTP and 65 rpm with 3 minutes easy. Alternate seated (odd reps) and standing for the last 30 seconds as needed. Builds power at threshold and above on short climbs.

name: Hill Repeats 6x5
desc: Six 5-minute climbs at 95% FTP and 70 rpm with 3 minutes descending recovery. Steady, controlled efforts just under threshold. An approachable climbing workout before progressing to 8x3.
src: Classic hill repeat session, easier variant

name: Belgian Bergs
desc: Ten short, punchy climbs of 45-90 seconds at 120-135% FTP, ridden standing at 70 rpm, separated by 3-4 minutes of rolling road at 65%. Simulates the cobbled bergs of a Flanders-style race. Hit each one hard from the bottom.

name: Rolling Hills
desc: Sixty minutes of continuous rolling terrain: 2-minute climbs at 92% FTP and 70 rpm linked by ramps up and down through tempo. Never fully recover; keep pressure on the pedals over each crest. Builds aerobic strength and pacing over undulating roads.

name: Torque Intervals 50-55rpm
desc: Five 6-minute strength-endurance intervals at 85% FTP and 50-55 rpm, seated, with 4 minutes at high cadence between. Low cadence, high force work builds muscular strength-endurance. Stop if knees complain and raise cadence.

name: Sweet Spot Torque
desc: Three 12-minute sweet spot intervals at 88% FTP and 58 rpm with 5 minutes recovery at normal cadence. Combines sweet spot aerobic load with low-cadence strength work. A climbing staple for long mountain days.

name: Alpine Climb Simulation
desc: Two long mountain passes of about 30 minutes each, with changing gradients from 78% to 92% FTP and cadence 60-72 rpm, separated by a 10-minute descent. Includes steeper hairpin sections and a hard final kilometre. Prepares you for long climbs in the Alps or Pyrenees.

name: Alpine Epic 3 Climbs
desc: A long mountain-stage simulation with three climbs of 20-30 minutes at 80-90% FTP and 60-70 rpm, linked by descents and valley roads at endurance pace. Total around 2.5 hours. Fuel as you would on a real mountain day.

name: Steep Steady Climb
desc: One continuous 40-minute steep climb at 83-88% FTP with cadence held at 60-65 rpm. Gradient barely relents, so the effort is about patience and constant torque. Simulates a brutal, steady-steep mountain road.
src: Inspired by the Mortirolo (steep, unrelenting gradient)

name: Climb with Kicks
desc: Three 10-minute climbs at 90% FTP and 65 rpm with a 20-second kick at 130% every 2 minutes. The kicks simulate steep ramps or attacks; return straight to climbing pace. 5 minutes recovery between climbs.

name: 20-Minute FTP Test
desc: Standard FTP test: after warm-up and openers, a 5-minute all-out blowout clears the fast-twitch reserve, then 10 minutes easy, then a 20-minute maximal even-paced effort. FTP is estimated as 95% of the 20-minute average power. ERG is released for test efforts.

name: Ramp Test
desc: One-minute steps rising by 6% FTP until you can no longer hold the power. Stay seated and keep cadence up; when cadence collapses the app ends the test automatically and drops you into the cool-down. New FTP is 75% of your best 1-minute power.
src: Standard incremental ramp test (MAP-based FTP estimate)

name: 8-Minute Test 2x8
desc: Two 8-minute maximal efforts with 10 minutes recovery between. Pace each evenly; FTP is estimated as 90% of the better of the two efforts. Shorter than the 20-minute test and less mentally demanding.

name: 5-Minute MAP Test
desc: A single maximal 5-minute effort after a thorough warm-up. Start strong but controlled and empty the tank in the final minute. The result approximates maximal aerobic power and anchors VO2max training zones.

name: 1-Minute Power Test
desc: A maximal 1-minute effort to gauge anaerobic capacity, with a second attempt after 15 minutes if the first felt mis-paced. Go hard from the start but avoid a full sprint in the first 10 seconds. Use the best result.

name: Critical Power Test 3+12
desc: Two all-out efforts of 3 and 12 minutes separated by 30 minutes easy riding. Together they allow estimation of critical power and W' (anaerobic work capacity). Pace both evenly to exhaustion.

name: Sprint Power Test
desc: Three 10-second maximal sprints with 5 minutes rest, one seated from moderate speed and two standing. Captures peak power for neuromuscular zone setting and tracking sprint progress.

name: Road Race Simulation
desc: A 90-minute race simulation: fast start, sustained tempo in the bunch, surges, two climbs, a breakaway attempt and a sprint finish. Efforts are unpredictable by design. Builds race-specific fitness and the ability to respond while fatigued.

name: Criterium Simulation
desc: Forty minutes of crit racing: hard 15-second accelerations out of corners every minute over a fast 85% base, a prime sprint at halfway and a sprint finish. Builds repeated-surge tolerance and fatigue-resistant speed.

name: Short Crit Simulation
desc: An easier 25-minute crit block: 15-second corner accelerations at 130% every minute on an 80% base, finishing with a sprint. A gentler introduction to repeated surges.

name: Fartlek Ride
desc: An hour of playful speed changes: tempo stretches, threshold pushes, short VO2 bursts and sprints, with no set pattern. Keeps the mind engaged while touching every intensity zone.
src: Swedish fartlek ("speed play") adapted for the bike

name: Gran Fondo Pacing
desc: A 2.5-hour long-day rehearsal: endurance riding at 65-70% FTP with three climbs of 10-15 minutes at 80-85%. Practise disciplined pacing and fuelling so you finish strong. Resist going over 85% on the climbs.

name: Time Trial Pacing 40min
desc: A 40-minute time-trial simulation paced the right way: controlled first 5 minutes at 95%, a long steady middle at 98%, and the final 5 minutes at 103%. Teaches even, negative-split pacing in an aero position.

name: Time Trial Pacing 20min
desc: A shorter 20-minute time-trial effort: first 3 minutes at 98%, 14 minutes at 100% and a strong finish at 105%, ending with a 15-second all-out to the line. Rehearses pacing for short TTs and hill climbs.

name: Long Climb with Attacks
desc: A 40-minute climb at 85% FTP and 70 rpm interrupted by a 30-second attack at 130% every 5 minutes, ending with an all-out summit sprint. Teaches you to absorb accelerations and return to climbing rhythm. A grand-tour style mountain-top finish.
src: Inspired by long Spanish mountain finishes with repeated attacks

name: Breakaway Simulation
desc: Simulates going up the road: a 1-minute attack to get clear, 15 minutes of breakaway pace at 92-95% with turns on the front, then a final 2-minute effort to hold off the chase. Ridden twice with 10 minutes recovery.

name: Short Race Simulation
desc: A 60-minute, lighter race simulation with tempo bunch riding, a few surges, one climb and a sprint finish. A good option early in the season or for riders new to racing.
src: Coach-standard road race simulation, reduced load
